claim: No upregulation of W09B7.2/F07B7.2 and Y102A5C.36 was detectable in sid-1(jam113[deletion]) animals by RT-qPCR.
source: but no upregulation was detectable in sid-1(jam113[deletion]) animals (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E)

claim: Changes in sdg-1 and sdg-2 mRNA levels persisted for more than 100 generations after restoration of SID-1.

claim: Changes in sdg-2 were observed in 9 of 21 published datasets examining RNA silencing factors.
source: while changes in sdg-2 were observed in 9 of 21 (Figure 5F)
evidence: This is supported by analysis of published datasets shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Depletion of downstream 22G RNAs targeting both sid-1 and sdg-1 was detectable upon loss of MUT-16.

claim: Both sid-1 and sdg-1 were among the top 500 genes targeted by 22G RNAs bound by HRDE-1/WAGO-9.

source: One, loss of HRDE-1/WAGO-9 increased sdg-1 RNA in whole animals (Ni et al., 2016; Figure 5F)

claim: Loss of HRDE-1/WAGO-9 increased sdg-1 RNA in dissected gonads.
source: One, loss of HRDE-1/WAGO-9 increased sdg-1 RNA in whole animals (Ni et al., 2016; Figure 5F) and in dissected gonads (Kim et al., 2021; Figure 5F)

claim: Loss of PRG-1 decreased sdg-1 RNA.
source: Two, loss of PRG-1 decreased sdg-1 RNA (Figure 5F)

claim: Loss of PRG-1 increased 22G RNAs that are antisense to sdg-1 in dissected gonads.

claim: The increase in sdg-1 22G RNA persisted in near-sterile animals that lack PRG-1.

claim: The increase in sdg-1 22G RNA in near-sterile prg-1(-) animals was eliminated upon additional loss of HRDE-1/WAGO-9.

claim: sdg-1 was identified as upregulated in animals lacking DEPS-1 using microarrays.
source: pioneering studies that used microarrays identified sdg-1 as upregulated in animals lacking the germ granule component DEPS-1 (Spike et al., 2008; Figure 5F)
evidence: This is cited from prior literature (Spike et al., 2008) and shown in Figure 5F.

claim: sdg-1 was identified as upregulated in animals lacking RDE-4 using microarrays.

evidence: This is cited from prior literature (Welker et al., 2007) and shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Animals that lack RDE-4 show a ~47.5-fold increase in sdg-1 RNA.
source: Animals that lack RDE-4 show a ~47.5-fold increase in sdg-1 RNA (Welker et al., 2007)
evidence: This is cited from prior literature (Welker et al., 2007).

evidence: This is cited from prior literature (Spike et al., 2008).

source: The sdg-1 gene is located within a retrotransposon (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This is supported by genomic analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The sdg-1 retrotransposon is within a duplicated ~40 kb region and has two recognizable paralogs.
source: The sdg-1 gene is located within a retrotransposon (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A) that is within a duplicated ~40 kb region and has two recognizable paralogs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: This is supported by genomic analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and 1B.

claim: There are no detectable SDG-1 homologs in species other than C. elegans.
source: However, there are no detectable SDG-1 homologs in species other than C. elegans, suggesting that it is a recently evolved gene

claim: AlphaFold is unable to predict a confident structure for SDG-1.
source: Potentially because of this lack of conservation, AlphaFold is unable to predict a confident structure for SDG-1 (CELE_F07B7.2 on the Database; Varadi et al., 2022)
evidence: This is stated based on AlphaFold predictions with citation.

claim: Tagging both sdg-1 loci with mCherry∆pi resulted in sdg-1::mCherry∆pi mRNA being ~16-fold higher than sdg-1 mRNA.

claim: Fluorescence from SDG-1::mCherry was observed in the germline of adult animals.

claim: Animals showed variation in SDG-1::mCherry expression between their two gonad arms.
source: However, animals showed variation in SDG-1::mCherry expression between their two gonad arms (Figure 6A, middle shows bright anterior [20% of animals] and right shows bright posterior [6% of animals])
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Unbiased passaging of self-progeny for more than 18 generations continuously preserved SDG-1::mCherry expression in an otherwise wild-type background.

claim: Reduced SDG-1::mCherry fluorescence was observed in mutants with reduced processing of intracellular dsRNA (eri-1(-)).
source: or reduced processing of intracellular dsRNA (Figure 6D, eri-1(-))

claim: An increase in SDG-1::mCherry fluorescence was observed in animals lacking MUT-16.
source: In contrast, we observed an increase in SDG-1::mCherry fluorescence in animals lacking MUT-16 (Figure 6D)

claim: Animals lacking RME-2 showed an increase in SDG-1::mCherry fluorescence.

claim: Short exposure to pos-1-dsRNA caused intermediate levels of silencing in wild-type animals and comparable intermediate silencing in sdg-1 mutant and sdg-1 overexpressing animals.
source: This short exposure to pos-1-dsRNA caused intermediate levels of silencing in wild-type animals and comparable intermediate silencing in sdg-1 mutant and sdg-1 overexpressing animals (Figure 7A)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: sid-1(-) animals exhibited enhanced mating-induced silencing.
source: We found that sid-1(-) animals exhibited enhanced mating-induced silencing (Figure 7B, top right:~50% off in sid-1(+) vs 100% off in sid-1(qt9[nonsense]))
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Animals lacking sdg-1 showed a small reduction in mating-induced silencing that was not statistically significant.
source: while animals lacking sdg-1 showed a small reduction in mating-induced silencing that was not statistically significant (Figure 7B, bottom right, ~40% off in sdg-1(+) vs ~30% off in sdg-1(jam232[deletion]))
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: SDG-1::mCherry was enriched in perinuclear foci in many animals.
source: SDG-1::mCherry was enriched in perinuclear foci in many animals (Figure 7C, top; 7 of 9 animals)

claim: SDG-1::mCherry re-localizes into the nucleus from the cytoplasm in the –1 oocyte.

evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 7D and Video 1.

claim: SDG-1::mCherry is excluded from the nucleus before the maternal and paternal pronuclei meet.
source: along with subsequent exclusion from the nucleus before the maternal and paternal pronuclei meet (Figure 7D, right and Video 2)
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 7D and Video 2.

claim: Dynamic entry into the nucleus followed by exclusion from the nucleus also occurred during early cell divisions in the developing embryo.
source: Such dynamic entry into the nucleus followed by exclusion from the nucleus also occurred during early cell divisions in the developing embryo (Videos 3 and 4)
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Videos 3 and 4.

claim: The timing of nuclear entry of SDG-1::mCherry coincides with nuclear envelope breakdown events that occur during fertilization and early development.
source: The timing of nuclear entry of SDG-1::mCherry coincides with the nuclear envelope breakdown events that occur during fertilization and early development (Huelgas-Morales and Greenstein, 2018)
evidence: This is stated as an inference with citation.

evidence: This is stated as part of the proposed model based on the findings.

source: In agreement with this proposal, SID-1 limits heritable RNA silencing because loss of SID-1 enhances mating-induced silencing (Figure 7B, top)
